description: Scale armor was widely used across the ancient world, especially in the Near East, Persia, Greece, and later Rome. It consisted of many small bronze, iron, or hardened-leather scales sewn or laced onto a textile or leather backing, giving the wearer strong protection while preserving more flexibility than a solid cuirass. Its construction was labor-intensive, but it was well suited to cavalry and elite infantry and remained popular for centuries because damaged scales could be replaced individually.
Body armor reinforced with bronze scales.
